pie.guia: How to upload your first raid
portada.que.1: Progress per attempt, where the group gets stuck, what kills each player, when the boss casts each attack and every player’s numbers: damage, healing, shields, deaths and rotation.
portada.que.2: Every player gets a page with all their raids: how they evolve, how they die, how they heal or support and their rotation, compared with their class and the group.
portada.que.3: An analysis of each night with recommendations for the group and for each player, written from the data (automatically with AI or by hand).
portada.que.4: Questlog logs are processed in your browser: only the stats of your group’s players are uploaded. Each group decides which raids are public.
portada.empezar.texto: You need the Questlog desktop app with its combat meter and a Discord account. Create your group, invite the others and upload your first night in a few minutes.
portada.empezar.guia: How to upload your first raid
guia.titulo: How to upload your first raid
guia.lede: From the Questlog app to your group’s page, in six steps. You need a Windows computer (the one you play on) and Chrome, Edge or Firefox.
guia.1: Play with the Questlog desktop app open and its combat meter on. Questlog saves every encounter in %APPDATA%\Questlog\aion-2; there is nothing to export. It only keeps the latest encounters, so upload the night before too many days go by.
guia.2: Press “Sign in with Discord” at the top right. It is only used to know who you are; nothing is posted to your Discord.
guia.3: In “My groups”, give it a name and an address (it will be /g/your-address). A new group is hidden and its raids are private: only its members see it until you change that.
guia.4: In the group settings, create an invite link and share it on your Discord. Roles: member (sees private raids), publisher (also uploads raids), admin (invites, changes roles and settings) and owner (can also delete the group).
guia.5: On the group page, “Upload a raid”: pick the %APPDATA%\Questlog\aion-2 folder, then the night (runs with 8 or more players are raids) and press “Calculate”. Everything is computed in your browser in a few seconds; check the summary, choose who can see it and upload it. If someone else in the group already uploaded the same night, the site detects it and lets you replace it.
guia.6: Each raid can be private (members only), by link (anyone with the address) or public (listed on the group page). To show the group on the home page, tick “visible” in its settings.
guia.extra.ia: AI analysis: a publisher can press “Analyze with AI” on a raid (once every 24 hours per raid); new raids are analyzed automatically if the site has AI enabled.
guia.extra.discord: Discord notice: with a webhook in the group settings, anyone can request their profile analysis from the player search and the notice reaches your channel.
guia.extra.pc: From the PC: an admin can create a token in the settings to publish with a script instead of the browser.
guia.extra.limite: Limit: each group can upload up to {n} new raids every 30 days (updating one already uploaded doesn’t count).
guia.problemas.1: “That folder doesn’t look like Questlog’s”: pick the aion-2 folder, the one that contains runs and encounters, not one of its subfolders.
guia.problemas.2: The night isn’t listed: Questlog only keeps the latest encounters; an old raid may be gone.
guia.problemas.3: “Couldn’t prepare the processor”: reload the page or try another desktop browser (Chrome, Edge or Firefox).
privacidad.lede: What DPS Aion stores, who sees it and how to ask for it to be deleted. It is a site made by players, free and without ads.
privacidad.raids.t: What is stored for each raid
privacidad.raids: The stats computed from the Questlog logs: the name, server and class of each character in the group, their gear (GS) and their numbers in each attempt (damage, healing, shields, damage taken, deaths and their causes, skills used, buffs and health over the fight), plus the boss, the date and the result. Raw logs are not uploaded: they are processed in the uploader’s browser or PC, and characters outside the group are not stored.
privacidad.cuenta: When you sign in with Discord, your name, avatar, email and Discord id are stored, and for each session the IP and browser (for session security). Each raid records which account uploaded it and which character recorded it; apart from that, your account is not linked to any in-game character. Nothing is posted to your Discord.
privacidad.quien: Each raid is private (group members only), by link (anyone with its address) or public. Player profiles only show the raids the viewer can see. A hidden group is not listed on the home page and doesn’t exist for non-members.
privacidad.terceros: The site is hosted on Vercel and the data is stored in Neon (Postgres). Sign-in is with Discord. If a group uses AI analysis, the raid summary (with character names, no account data) is sent to DeepSeek to write it. The “Request analysis” notice sends the player’s name and numbers to the group’s Discord and, if the group turns it on, every new raid sends a summary to that same channel (boss, group figures, and the headline and recommendations of the analysis, which may name characters).
privacidad.cookies: Only two: the session cookie (if you sign in) and the language you choose. No ads and no third-party analytics. Your browser also remembers which profiles you asked to have analyzed.
privacidad.borrar.t: Deleting data and hiding your name
privacidad.borrar: Whoever uploaded a raid or a group admin can delete it or make it private; the owner can delete the whole group with all its raids. You can leave a group at any time. To stop your character from appearing, ask the admin of their group; if they don’t answer, or to delete your account, write to {c} with the character’s name and server.
privacidad.condiciones: Only upload raids you or your group played, don’t upload fake data and don’t use the site to single anyone out: the analyses are advice to improve. The site is provided as is, without warranties, and may change or close; usage limits (such as {n} new raids every 30 days per group) may be adjusted. Aion 2 and Questlog belong to their owners; this site is not affiliated with either.
mec.sinDatos: This raid was uploaded before the site worked out mechanic mistakes. Upload it again (replacing it) and they will show up here.
mec.vacio: No attack in this raid hit only part of the group often enough to compare.
mec.rank.t: Who takes hits the rest avoid
mec.rank.nota: Only attacks that do not hit the whole group count, and a player is not charged with the attacks that target them every time. “Expected” is the number of hits they would have taken at the same rate as everyone else. This is inferred from the data, not a game rule: the log does not say which attacks can be dodged, and whoever tanks or fights in melee is usually more exposed.
mec.mapa.nota: Each cell: times the attack hit the player, out of the times it went out while they were alive; more colour means more often. ▲ hit far more than the rest · ▽ far less · ◎ its fixed target (usually whoever tanks), not counted as a mistake. The deadliest attacks come first.
mec.celda: {j}: hit {n} of {de} times (at the rate of the rest it would be {esp})
mec.celda.alto: {j}: hit {n} of {de} times, far more than the rest (it would be {esp})
mec.celda.bajo: {j}: hit {n} of {de} times, far less than the rest (it would be {esp})
mec.celda.objetivo: {j}: fixed target of this attack ({n} of {de} times)
mec.celda.nada: {j}: dead every time it went out
mec.resto: Attacks that hit the whole group or have too little data ({n})
rep.sinDatos: This raid was uploaded before the site reviewed each death. Upload it again (replacing it) and the review will show up here.
rep.parcial: Only {n} of the {de} deaths have the data of their last 10 s.
rep.tabla.nota: One hit: a single hit took them out, either from 80% health or more or because the hit removes 80% of their maximum health at once; that is a mechanic, no healing fixes it. Burst: they were fine 3 s earlier and fell to several hits in a row. Worn down: they had been low for 3 s or more. “With a defensive ready”: they died to a burst or worn down while a self-shield was probably available. This is an inference from the data, with fixed thresholds.
rep.lista.nota: Each attempt, in the order they fell. The line is their health over the last 10 s; next to it, what they took and the healing they got in that time, and how many teammates were still alive. Healers are clerics and chanters. A defensive's cooldown is inferred from the shortest time between two uses by that player.
rep.vida.aria: Health: {a}% ten seconds earlier and {b}% before the final hit
ven.sinDatos: This raid was uploaded before the site measured damage windows. Upload it again (replacing it) and they will show up here.
ven.rot.nota: The stagger bar broke {n} times in {i} attempts ({s} s in total). DPS is damage to the boss per second alive, inside those breaks and in the rest of those same attempts; the multiplier says how much it goes up. ▲ goes up far more than the group, ▽ far less: it is a comparison (only with 3 breaks or more), and healers and tanks normally go up less.
ven.rot.ninguna: The boss stagger bar did not break in any attempt.
ven.th.pct: Share of their damage in the break
ven.deb.nota: Effects of their skills each player keeps on the boss: share of the time of their attempts they are up (counting time spent dead) and share of the stagger time. Only those reaching 10%.
seg.nota: This raid ({m} attempts) compared with the previous one on this boss ({n} attempts). Figures are per attempt, so nights of different length can be compared. A number getting better does not prove the advice was followed: only that it got better.
seg.sinTasas: One of the two raids has no per-attack hit detail, so only deaths are compared for each attack.
seg.recos.nota: Each recommendation of the previous analysis is measured by the attacks it named: deaths per attempt and, when the data is there, how often the attack hit someone when it came out.
seg.recos.vacio: The previous raid has no analysis, so there are no recommendations to follow up: only the figures are compared.
seg.sinAtaques: It names no attack that can be measured
seg.ataque.noAntes: did not show up in the previous raid
seg.ataque.noAhora: did not show up in this raid
seg.jug.t: Each player against their previous raid
seg.jug.nota: Only those who were in both raids. The last column shows the attacks their personal advice named.
ajustes.aviso.raids: Post every new raid to that channel
ajustes.aviso.nota: When a new raid is uploaded, a message arrives with the boss, attempts, deaths, the headline of the analysis and its first recommendations, with the link to the raid. The message is written in the language you are viewing this page in when you save.
cmp.sep.notaKill: Each attempt is compared with the kill (attempt {i}).
cmp.sep.notaMejor: Each attempt is compared with the one that got furthest (attempt {i}, {p}%).
cmp.sep.nota: The comparison is at equal progress: at every 5% of the boss’s health that both reached, how many seconds they took and how many deaths they had. An attempt falls behind at the first point where it has 3 more deaths or is 15% (and 10 s) slower; if it never does, it was on par up to that point and fell apart afterwards. “Died earlier” lists who was already down at that point but not in the best attempt: whoever goes down first may be the target of a mechanic. It is an inference with fixed thresholds.
cmp.cuenta.ninguno: {n} on par until they fell apart
cmp.tabla.t: Time and deaths to each % of the boss
cmp.tabla.nota: Seconds to take each 10% of the boss’s health and deaths so far († = deaths). In red, what is clearly worse than attempt {i} at that same point.
cmp.jug.t: Who goes down earlier than in the best attempt
cmp.jug.nota: In how many attempts each player was already dead at the point where the attempt falls behind (or at its last point in common) but not in {i}. Only repeat cases. They may be the target of a mechanic: it is not always their mistake.
jefe.lede.kill: First killed on {d}. Here are all the group’s raids against this boss, together.
jefe.lede.sinKill: No kill yet: the best attempt reached {p}. Here are all the group’s raids against this boss, together.
jefe.noches.nota: Each grey dot is an attempt (% of the boss’s health taken); the large dot is the best one of that raid, and the line joins them. A kill is shown in green. The median is that of the attempts that passed 5%: if it goes up, the group gets far more often, not just once.
jefe.muro.nota: {n} attempts without a kill that passed 5%, by the % of the boss’s health taken when they fell. The letters mark attacks that, according to the data, always come out at the same % of health (below): if a wall matches one, it is probably a phase the group does not get through.
jefe.cro.nota: Inferred from the {n} attempts that passed 5%: the first cast of each attack in each attempt (median), in seconds and in % of health taken. “Comes out in” counts the attempts that got that far into the fight. “By time”: it almost always comes out at the same second; “by health”: almost always at the same % (a phase change). “Repeats”: the time between two casts in a row is almost always the same. It is an inference with fixed thresholds: the game does not say what triggers each attack.
jefe.causas.tabla: Deaths per attempt for each attack
jefe.causas.nota: The attacks with the most deaths across all raids, with their deaths per attempt in each one ({n}). If it goes down, the group handles it better; “—”: it killed nobody that night.
jefe.causas.notaUltimas: The attacks with the most deaths across all raids, with their deaths per attempt in the last {n}. If it goes down, the group handles it better; “—”: it killed nobody that night.
jefe.pie: Everything comes from the raids of this group that you can see. Raids uploaded later are added automatically.
bx.sinDatos: This raid was uploaded before the site read specializations and the buffs each player receives. Upload it again (replacing it) and they will show here.
bx.esp.nota: The specialization options each player chose for each skill, numbered in the game’s order (2·4·5 = options 2, 4 and 5). They are inferred from the id the skill is cast with; the game does not state them. ● marks whoever differs from the majority of their class; amber marks skills with no majority. It does not say which option is better: with so few players per class, damage depends on much more.
bx.distinta: Differs from the majority of their class
bx.buf.nota: The share of their time alive in which each player had each buff from a teammate, in the attempts where they received it, compared with the others who get the same buff from the same caster (usually their party). Whoever has it much less (25% below the others’ median and 8 points or more) is probably out of its range, for example the healer who stays behind the tank. It is an inference.
bx.buf.bajo: {j} had {h} from {l} {p} of their time alive; the others, {m}.
bx.buf.ninguno: Nobody receives a buff much less than their teammates.
bx.perfil.t: Specializations compared with others of their class ({c})
bx.perfil.nota: Their most recent raid compared with the most recent one of every other player of their class in the raids you can see (the date is under each name).
bx.perfil.solo: Their specializations in their most recent raid; there are no other players of their class to compare with yet.
raid.recoJug.nota: Click a name to open their card.
cmp.sep.corto: Where each attempt falls behind the best one: by deaths or by pace.
cmp.jug.corto: Who was already down where the attempt fell behind, but not in {i}.
rep.tabla.corto: Each death, sorted: one hit, burst or worn down.
rep.lista.corto: Each attempt in the order they fell: health, damage taken and healing received in the last 10 s.
mec.rank.corto: Who takes more hits than expected from attacks that do not hit the whole group.
mec.mapa.corto: Times each attack hit the player, out of the times it went out while they were alive. ▲ far more than the rest · ▽ far less · ◎ fixed target.
ven.rot.corto: The bar broke {n} times in {i} attempts ({s} s). DPS per second alive, inside and outside the breaks; ▲/▽ goes up far more or less than the group.
ven.deb.corto: How long each player keeps their effects on the boss, overall and during the break.
bx.esp.corto: Specialization options for each skill (2·4·5 = options 2, 4 and 5). ● differs from their class; amber, no majority.
bx.buf.corto: Who gets a teammate’s buff much less than the rest: probably out of its range.
rep.res: Group: {n} deaths; {g} in one hit ({p}), {r} in a burst and {d} worn down.
rep.barra.aria: {j}: {n} deaths; {g} in one hit, {r} in a burst, {d} worn down
mec.det: {r} taken · {e} expected · {m} deaths from these attacks
mec.mapa.solo: Only the attacks where someone gets hit far more than the rest ({n} of {de}).
ven.deb.top: The 3 each player keeps up the most.
